Share on X Telegram Gospel singer Tope Alabi has threatened legal action against a Canada-based pastor over social media allegations linking her to the death of fellow gospel minister Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings.
Alabi’s solicitors, Oakmount Legal Practitioners, issued a cease-and-desist letter dated October 24, demanding that the operator of the Facebook page Pastor Tayo Ministries remove the publications, retract the allegations and issue a public apology within 24 hours.
The letter identified the page operator as Tayo Kumuyi, also known as Pastor Tayo Ministries, and accused him of publishing claims between October 20 and 24 linking Alabi to murder and ritual killings involving Toluwanisings and other gospel ministers.
“These statements accuse our client of murder and of ritual killing. There is no more serious allegation that can be made against a person, least of all a minister of the gospel. They are false in every particular,” the solicitors stated.
They said Alabi had publicly and privately mourned Toluwanisings and denied any involvement in his death or that of anyone else.
The lawyers accused the page operator of exploiting public grief to damage the singer’s reputation, adding that presenting the allegations as spiritual revelations did not exempt them from legal scrutiny.
The letter also cited a subsequent post allegedly directed at Alabi after she issued a public notice warning against defamation on October 23.
Quoting the post, the solicitors wrote: “Tope Alabi, no letter will save you from my hand. Your only option is leaving your hiding place.”
They described the statement as a threat that could serve as evidence of continued harassment and defamation.
The solicitors said the publications could harm Alabi’s reputation, professional standing and ministry, noting that the allegations had attracted comments and shares, with some readers appearing to believe the claims.
They demanded the removal of the disputed posts, an end to further publication of the allegations, withdrawal of requests for others to share them and preservation of relevant evidence, including recordings, messages, drafts and account records.
They also requested an unreserved public retraction and apology on the same Facebook page, to remain pinned for 14 consecutive days and receive prominence comparable to the original publications.
The letter further asked the recipient to disclose the factual basis for any allegations maintained and clarify whether the claims had been reported to the Nigeria Police Force or another competent authority.
The lawyers warned that failure to comply within 24 hours could result in court action seeking an injunction, damages and legal costs. They also cited possible complaints to Meta Platforms and referrals of the alleged threats to law enforcement.
They clarified that the legal notice was not intended to prevent truthful reporting, lawful investigations or legitimate commentary protected by law.
Toluwanisings, whose real name was Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, died on October 14, 2026, aged 41. Alabi publicly mourned the gospel minister following his death.
The allegations against Alabi and the claims of threatening messages were presented in the solicitors’ letter and have not been independently verified.
